title: The Club Alabam show, uniforms and why it closed
summary: The Alabam was a lavish nightclub with floor shows and a good-quality, well-rehearsed band, and closed as summer slowed business.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So we're back at the Club Alabam with Billy Fowler, and you've just remembered that the drummer was Walter Johnson.
Were you in the pit or on-stage.
This was a nightclub. A beautiful nightclub. I think it was on 54th Street. [SIC: 44th?] I don't know whether it was...
So it was a whole bandstand with a show?

Oh yes. A beautiful bandstand. A big bandstand, a big dance floor. A great big show, a production. They changed it every six months. See, they put on what you call an extravaganza. They had showgirls just to pose, they had chorus girls to dance... Oh, it was beautiful. An elaborate club. And it was a big club...
Oh sure. Oh yeah. Everything looked good. Everything.

Oh yeah. Everything was good quality. Good leader. Good conductor. He knew what he was doing, you know? Yeah, he was very good. Everything went down beautifully. Then they closed up. At the good jobs,
What was the reason for the closing?
Well, summer was coming on. You know, business gets slower.
In those days, New York shut up July and August. The department stores closed and everything.
Sure. There was no air conditioning in those days. But I think they were getting kind of short on the money anyway.
